description: The provided chart is a nested donut chart illustrating the distribution of responses across two levels of ambiguity — “Ambiguity 1 (Outer)” and “Ambiguity 2 (Inner)” — in the context of social engineering attacks, likely as part of an experiment or survey from the paper “Defending Against Social Engineering Attacks in the Age of LLMs.” The outer ring, labeled “Ambiguity 1,” is divided into three segments: “Deceived” (67.6%, dark red), “Partially” (31.6%, gold), and “Not Deceived” (10.5%, green). The inner ring, “Ambiguity 2,” mirrors the same categories but with different proportions: “Deceived” (57.9%, dark red), “Partially” (23.5%, gold), and “Not Deceived” (8.8%, green). Both rings use identical color coding for corresponding categories, as clarified by the two separate legends on the right. The chart visually emphasizes that deception rates are higher under Ambiguity 1 than Ambiguity 2, with the “Deceived” category dominating both rings, while “Not Deceived” remains the smallest segment in each. The percentages are displayed directly on the chart segments, and the overall design suggests a comparison of susceptibility to deception under varying levels of ambiguity.
